_note: Slim slices carry every field the paper's headline numbers are computed from. The full artifacts (15 MB each) additionally carry output_with_memory / output_without_memory, the raw model text. Those are NOT tracked here for size, but their sha256 is recorded so a reviewer can verify any copy they are given is the one the paper used. Keeping the full text matters: a stored digest alone would block every later re-scoring under a corrected verifier.
_verified: All headline numbers re-derived from the slim slices alone on 2026-09-29 and reproduce exactly.

scicode_scaleup.why_untracked: repo convention: raw endpoint outputs stay untracked (.gitignore results/**); the slim slice carries every field the reported numbers are computed from, and the sha256 above lets a reviewer verify any copy they are given is the one used.
scicode_scaleup.dropped_fields: stderr_tail and detail (size). MEASURED, not recalled: FULL row keys minus SLIM row keys = ['detail','stderr_tail'] exactly. 🔴 CORRECTION (2026-09-30): this field previously claimed the slim slice dropped 'per-arm raw model text' which 'the full artifact retains on disk so later re-scoring stays possible'. THAT WAS FALSE IN BOTH HALVES. There is no model-text key in the full artifact at all -- scripts/scicode_pilot.py's run_arm() records response_chars=len(content) and DISCARDS content, and P1Client was constructed with no cache=, so no completion was persisted anywhere (verified: 0 of 12,023 entries across results/**/*cache*.jsonl key benchmark='scicode'; the same scan keys 12,023 as 'longmemeval_v2', which is the positive control proving the scan can find data). Later re-scoring of SciCode is therefore NOT possible from this artifact and requires re-running the 924 arm-runs. scripts/scicode_to_schema.py records this per row via schema.OUTPUT_NOT_RETAINED_SENTINEL plus a measured provenance.response_chars_<arm>, which is a PERSISTENCE gap and must never be conflated with the SWE-bench licence embargo.
